author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This parser reads Symantec DLP incidents, sent as CEF over syslog to the data collector by a Log to a Syslog Server response rule on the Enforce Server. Each incident goes to the third-party alert schema.
notes:
Setup:
- Send incidents with a Log to a Syslog Server response rule on the Enforce Server.
- DLP has no fixed syslog layout: paste the CEF message from Broadcom knowledge base article 256282, or the longer one in README.md, into the rule's Message field.

Field mapping:
- The parser reads the keys in any order and skips any that are missing.
- Each incident goes to the third-party alert schema: INCIDENT_ID as alert_id, the policy as the title, SEVERITY (High, Medium, Low or Info) as severity, BLOCKED=yes as the BLOCKED action, the endpoint user (or application user or sender), machine and IP as the source, DESTINATION_IP as the destination, and an http or https URL as destination_url.
- Rules, channel, recipients, match count, status, detection server, attachment, location and the incident snapshot link go to additional_data.

Time:
- The event time is the syslog header time: RFC 5424, or RFC 3164 with no year or zone, read as UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the shape of the KB 256282 message, with values from Broadcom's response action variable pages.

Testing:
- Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15 (91 of 91 fields matched the emulator, in each of 3 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 6 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- DLP doesn't escape the values it fills in, so a | in a policy name breaks the header and a doubled backslash, as in a UNC path, reads as one.
- Broadcom KB 159680 caps messages at 1,024 characters.
- System events (Manager.properties syslog) aren't covered.
